english: Consider the hyperbola $H:\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{5}=1$ and the parabola $C:y^{2}=12x$. Exactly two normals to $H$ are tangents to $C$; let them touch $C$ at the points $Q_{1}$ and $Q_{2}$. Then the length $Q_{1}Q_{2}$ is ______.
hindi: अतिपरवलय $H:\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{5}=1$ तथा परवलय $C:y^{2}=12x$ पर विचार कीजिए। $H$ के ठीक दो अभिलम्ब $C$ की स्पर्श रेखाएँ हैं; माना कि ये $C$ को बिन्दुओं $Q_{1}$ तथा $Q_{2}$ पर स्पर्श करते हैं। तब लम्बाई $Q_{1}Q_{2}$ ______ है।
solution: So $\cos\theta<0$: $P$ is on the left branch (no normal at a right-branch point works). With $u=-\cos\theta>0$: $1-u^{2}=\dfrac56u\Rightarrow 6u^{2}+5u-6=0\Rightarrow u=\dfrac23$
solution_full: Take $P(2\sec\theta,\sqrt5\tan\theta)$ on $H$ ($a=2$, $b=\sqrt5$, $a^{2}+b^{2}=9$). The normal at $P$ is $\dfrac{a x}{\sec\theta}+\dfrac{b y}{\tan\theta}=a^{2}+b^{2}$, i.e. $2x\cos\theta+\sqrt5\,y\cot\theta=9$.

For $\sin\theta\ne0$ this is $y=mx+k$ with $m=-\dfrac{2\sin\theta}{\sqrt5}$ and $k=\dfrac{9\tan\theta}{\sqrt5}$. (At the vertices the normal is the $x$-axis, which is the axis of $C$ and not a tangent.)
A line $y=mx+k$ ($m\ne0$) touches $y^{2}=4\cdot3\,x$ if and only if $k=\dfrac3m$, i.e. $km=3$.

The left side has the sign of $\cos\theta$, so $\cos\theta<0$: only points of the left branch qualify. Put $u=-\cos\theta>0$: $\dfrac{1-u^{2}}{u}=\dfrac56\Rightarrow 6u^{2}+5u-6=0\Rightarrow(3u-2)(2u+3)=0\Rightarrow u=\dfrac23$.
Then $\sec\theta=-\dfrac32$ and $\sin^{2}\theta=\dfrac59$, so $P=\left(-3,\ \pm\dfrac52\right)$; check: $\dfrac94-\dfrac{25}{4\cdot5}=1$. These are exactly two points, hence exactly two normals.

At $P\left(-3,\dfrac52\right)$: $\tan\theta=-\dfrac{\sqrt5}{2}$, $\sin\theta=-\dfrac{\sqrt5}{3}$, $m=\dfrac23$, $k=\dfrac92$: the normal is $y=\dfrac23x+\dfrac92$. At $P\left(-3,-\dfrac52\right)$ the normal is $y=-\dfrac23x-\dfrac92$.
The point of contact of $y=mx+\dfrac3m$ with $y^{2}=12x$ is $\left(\dfrac{3}{m^{2}},\dfrac{6}{m}\right)$: $Q_{1}=\left(\dfrac{27}{4},9\right)$ and $Q_{2}=\left(\dfrac{27}{4},-9\right)$.
originality_note: New: normals of a hyperbola that are tangents of a parabola; the tangency condition forces cos(theta) < 0, so only the left branch, away from the parabola, contributes (way 5). Closest known: common tangents of a hyperbola and a parabola. Different because: a normal (not a tangent) of H is matched with a tangent of C, and the sign argument that excludes the whole right branch is the key step.
blueprint_concepts: Tangent to the parabola: point, slope and parametric forms

concept_use.Tangent and normal for Hyperbola: The normal to H at (2 sec theta, sqrt5 tan theta), 2x cos theta + sqrt5 y cot theta = 9, gives the slope and intercept of the line.
concept_use.Tangent to the parabola: point, slope an: The tangency condition k = 3/m for y^2 = 12x and the point of contact (3/m^2, 6/m) give the equation for theta and the points Q1, Q2.

justification: Two ideas linked: the parametric normal of a hyperbola and the tangency condition of a parabola, with a sign argument on the branch. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q2 (L3) on common tangents of a conic and a parabola, in numerical form.
